quotelist.quote: Salomon SAS is a French sports equipment manufacturing company headquartered in Annecy, France. It was founded in 1947 by François Salomon in the heart of the French Alps.

citation.url_with_text_link: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salomon_Group#,Salomon SAS is a French,heart of the French Alps
citation.reasoning: Wikipedia's Salomon Group article is well-sourced and consistent with all other historical sources. Founding date, location and name are undisputed facts.

quotelist.quote: Salomon is owned by Finnish retail conglomerate Amer Sports, along with Wilson, Atomic, Precor, and Arc'teryx, among others.
The Salomon Group was purchased by Adidas in 1997 and the official name was changed to Adidas-Salomon AG. Adidas then later sold the company to Amer Sports in 2005.

citation.reasoning: Wikipedia is consistent with all other sources (Sneakerjagers, Skiing History) on corporate history. The ownership by Amer Sports and prior Adidas ownership is well-established public knowledge.

quotelist.quote: Salomon's Annecy Design Center is the brand's global headquarters.
Commercial skis like the QST line are designed here, but built at the much larger and more efficient AMER factory in Altenmarkt, Austria.

citation.reasoning: Powder Magazine's factory tour article is a credible first-hand source for Salomon's design and manufacturing operations. Confirms Annecy as design/HQ, Altenmarkt Austria for manufacturing at scale.

quotelist.quote: Marketing for Salomon Snowboards is based in Portland, Oregon, near Mount Hood, while design and development takes place at the base of the French Alps, in Annecy, France.
Salomon released their first snowboard in 1997 after several years of development.
In 2008, the Salomon SickStick snowboard won the Volvo SportsDesign Award for Eco Design in the boardsports category.

citation.reasoning: Wikipedia Salomon Snowboards page provides verified historical dates for the snowboard division, marketing location and the eco-design award. Cross-referenced with Salomon's own about page.

quotelist.quote: The HPS Series, which began with the Sickstick in 2008, has been expanded and developed under the careful guidance of Wolle Nyvelt.

citation.reasoning: Snowboard Magazine is one of the most authoritative specialist snowboard publications. The article directly confirms the HPS series origin year and Wolle Nyvelt's continuous role.

quotelist.quote: The Hillside Project is Salomon's vision of powder riding through the lens of their riders and the shaping expertise of Wolle Nyvelt.

Not all snow is created equal; powder in the Cascades is very different from powder in Niseko. Some people want to turn, others want to spin off a natural feature. This is the concept behind the Hillside Project—different boards for different terrain, snow, and riding styles.

citation.reasoning: Whitelines is one of the UK's most established and credible snowboard publications. This directly defines the HPS concept and design philosophy.

quotelist.quote: After giving the HPS treatment to Annie Boulanger and Takaharu Nakai, this year the honour goes to Louif Paradis.
Once arguably the most accomplished rail rider of his generation, he's since transitioned gracefully into a freerider extraordinaire – and the Salomon HPS Louis Paradis reflects that.
Tested and selected for our top 100 snowboard products of the year: the Salomon HPS Louif Paradis

citation.reasoning: Whitelines' 2021/22 review confirms the model's first introduction season (2021/22), the predecessor HPS models, Louif's rider background, and the Whitelines 100 award. This is a primary specialist media source.

quotelist.quote: HPS Louif Paradis $699.95 Sizes: 156, 160, 164

citation.reasoning: Snowboard Magazine published this for the 2026 season quiver. This confirms the 2026 model's size range shift (156/160/164) and MSRP of $699.95 USD, useful for comparison with the 2024 model being researched.

quotelist.quote: Louif Paradis, c'est une légende du snowboard québécois.

citation.reasoning: Canadian specialty retailer blog confirms Louif Paradis' identity as a Québécois snowboarding legend. Consistent with all other sources.

quotelist.quote: Louif describes his riding as hybrid, often combining elements of powder and manufactured structures, blending both street and freeride skills.

Using his shaping expertise and Lou's critical feedback during the proto process, Wolle created this tapered directional board built for freestyle tactics in deep terrain, satisfying Lou's hybrid demand.

citation.reasoning: Salomon's official US product page is the primary authoritative source for design philosophy and rider description. This is the manufacturer's own voice and carries the highest credibility for non-metric attributes.

quotelist.quote: "The main focus for me when creating shapes with riders is purely listening to them in what they want." – Wolfgang Nyvelt
Each board rides as cleanly as it looks—responsive, poppy, flexible, forgiving, and exceedingly elegant.

citation.reasoning: Snowboard Magazine's first-look at the 2024 HPS quiver is one of the best specialist editorial sources on ride character and design philosophy. The direct Wolle Nyvelt quote is highly credible.

quotelist.quote: Best for All-Mountain, Freeride, Expert, Flex - Medium

citation.reasoning: Salomon's official US page rates the board as Expert level and Medium flex — in direct disagreement with the merchant's "Intermediate-Advanced" and "Soft" ratings. As the manufacturer, this source is the highest authority for such attributes on an objective scale, but flex perception is somewhat subjective.

quotelist.quote: It's built for advanced snowboarders who value stability, precision, and responsiveness but still want a board that feels playful underfoot.

We like the HPS Louif Paradis for how it connects freeride stability with freestyle creativity. The Popster core adds snap and pop, while bamboo and cork rails absorb chatter and keep the board feeling damp at speed.

citation.reasoning: Backcountry.com is a major, reputable US outdoor retailer with well-written editorial descriptions. Their description of target rider and ride character is informed and specific, making it a credible secondary source for ride experience attributes.

quotelist.quote: Pop: ABC Wrapper construction uses lively bamboo for explosive ollies and reactive turns, combined with Popster and Salomon's light and snappy Ghost Green Core for maximum load.
Float: A tapered tail and directional shape combined with rock out camber provide ultimate float and maneuverability in deep snow.

citation.reasoning: Comor Sports is a reputable Canadian specialty retailer. Their key performance highlights (pop, float) are consistent with Salomon's own marketing language, suggesting they are derived from official spec sheets.

quotelist.quote: Rock Out Camber – Flat between your bindings for stability, camber near the feet for response, and rocker on the tip/tail for pressability.
Tapered Directional – Tail width is slightly tapered (2-20mm). This loosens up turning initiation and improves floatation in deeper snow without sacrificing edge hold on hardpack.
Quadralizer Sidecut – Explosive combination of Equalizer and Quadratic sidecuts allows high speed carving as well as superior edge control in tight spots.

citation.reasoning: evo.com is a highly reputable snowboard specialty retailer. Their specifications are drawn directly from Salomon's own spec sheets. These are manufacturer-verbatim descriptions of camber, shape, and sidecut.

quotelist.quote: The Salomon HPS - Louif Paradis Snowboard features a distinctive blunt nose and tail in a charger powder design with 20mm of setback and a deep tip rocker for float.

citation.url_with_text_link: https://www.evo.com/snowboards/salomon-hps-louif-paradis-snowboard-2022#,distinctive blunt nose and tail,deep tip rocker for float
citation.reasoning: evo's 2024 model listing (the same as 2022 listing URL) confirms the blunt nose/tail design and setback specification. These are consistent across all sources and seasons.

quotelist.quote: No matter which size you go for, the nose is half a centimetre wider than the tail. It's subtle, but effective when you're railing a turn on hard-pack or trying to stay on top of things in the powder.

citation.url_with_text_link: https://whitelines.com/snowboard-gear/reviews/snowboards/salomon-hps-louis-paradis-2021-2022.html#,the nose is half a centimetre,in the powder
citation.reasoning: Whitelines' review provides the nose/tail taper measurement (5mm) and its practical effect. This is a specialist independent review, giving it high credibility for ride feel observations.

quotelist.quote: Salomon's a brand that likes to get techy with its profiles, and the one on the Salomon HPS Louif Paradis is divided into seven sections.

What you've essentially got, though, is a 'camber between the feet, rocker at each end' configuration, which offers plenty of pop with more margin for error (and opportunities for a butter session) than any classic camber.
As for the sidecut itself, it's Salomon's proprietary blend of straight sections and specially-positioned curves that holds an edge like no-one's business.

citation.reasoning: Whitelines specialist review confirms the 7-section profile complexity, camber/rocker configuration, and their assessment of edge hold quality. High credibility specialist source.

quotelist.quote: All-mountain freestyle is a hard niche to do well, but the Salomon HPS - Louif Paradis Snowboard has some excellent inspiration in it's namesake rider.
The Popster core and ABC Wrapper construction with snappy bamboo boosts your pop off lips and the flex is stiff enough to land those big off-piste jumps with ease.

Popster: The core is strategically milled inside of the insert packs, allowing the board to flex more naturally underfoot and transfer energy into the nose and tail for added pop.

citation.reasoning: Salomon's official US website is the highest authority on core construction technology names and descriptions. These are technical marketing claims from the manufacturer.

quotelist.quote: Salomon's Popster tech shapes the core to maximise the natural snap of the wood. To do this the wood core is thicker at the centre of the board then tapers out to thinner sections then thickens again towards the nose and tail, this creates an insane amount of powerful pop!
For even more pop, Ghost Carbon Stringers are placed from tip to tail. This will enhance stability at high speeds and will feel mellow for easy maneuverability.
